finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches any URL that merely contains the substring "example.io", so an unauthenticated client can make the server issue a GET to arbitrary internal or external hosts and receive the response body.
finding.source: Query or form parameter `logo`, read at main.go:31 via r.FormValue("logo"). Any client that can reach port 8081 controls it.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36 using the default client, which follows redirects. The response body is copied back to the client at main.go:38.

trace.note: /logo is registered on the default mux with no auth middleware.
raw := r.FormValue("logo"); value is attacker-supplied and not normalized.
Only check is !strings.Contains(raw, "example.io"), a substring match on the whole string rather than a hostname comparison.
http.Get(raw) has no scheme, host, IP, or port restriction and follows redirects.
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the fetched body to the attacker, making this a full-response SSRF rather than blind.

finding.guards_checked: Substring check at line 32 does not parse the URL, so it does not constrain the host. Bypasses such as http://127.0.0.1:6379/?example.io or http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io pass the check. Redirects are unrestricted, so an allowed-looking host can 30x to an internal address. Scheme is unrestricted, but Go's client rejects file:// and other non-HTTP schemes, so practical reach is http/https. No error check at line 36: a failed Get leaves resp nil and line 37 panics (crash, not SSRF).

verdict.guard_found: Only guard is the substring check at main.go:32 (`!strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")`). It does not parse the URL or compare the hostname, so it does not close the finding. No auth middleware exists on the /logo path.
verdict.reason: Trace note at main.go:42 is wrong: line 42 registers /cdn, not /logo (the /logo registration is at line 43). Under the rule that a misdescribed trace line makes the verdict REFUTED, this is REFUTED, but the underlying bug is real: main.go:31 takes `logo` from the request, main.go:32 is only a substring check, and main.go:36 calls http.Get(raw) with the default client, which follows redirects, with the body returned at main.go:38. The finding should be reissued with the line-42 citation corrected to line 43, and it would then be CONFIRMED.
